title: peer_rate_limiter uses std::sync::Mutex in async session: O(N) work under blocking lock
description: session.rs PeeringShared.peer_rate_limiter is an Arc<std::sync::Mutex<PeerRateLimiter>>. PeerRateLimiter::check() does O(N-peers) eviction work under that mutex (the retain call). With many concurrent sessions, any session calling check() holds a blocking mutex while iterating all peer buckets, blocking the tokio thread for all other sessions waiting on the lock. Trigger: high-volume peering with many concurrent peer IPs. Bad behavior: async tasks block on sync mutex, reducing throughput and potentially causing latency spikes. Should use tokio::sync::Mutex or restructure eviction.
